name: Infertility Evaluation, Ovulation Induction and Assisted Reproductive Technology

reference.source: Gynaecology by Ten Teachers 21st Edition / ESHRE Guidelines on Infertility
clinicalPearls: Infertility is defined as failure to conceive after twelve months of regular unprotected intercourse
Mid-luteal day 21 serum progesterone level above thirty nanomoles per liter confirms normal ovulation
Anti-Müllerian hormone produced by granulosa cells of preantral follicles reflects functional ovarian reserve
Letrozole aromatase inhibitor is first-line medical therapy for ovulation induction in anovulatory PCOS
Intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) overcomes severe male factor infertility and fertilization failure
reference.pathophysiology: Subfertility arises from male factors (30-40%), ovulatory disorders (25-30%), tubal or peritoneal disease (20-25%), and unexplained etiologies (15-20%). Ovulatory failure commonly reflects hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian axis dysregulation in PCOS. Tubal obstruction follows salpingitis or endometriosis. Assisted reproduction bypasses mechanical barriers through gamete micromanipulation and controlled ovarian stimulation.
additionalDifferentials: Tubal occlusion from prior PID versus pelvic endometriosis
additionalInvestigations: Semen analysis according to WHO 2021 reference manual
Mid-luteal serum progesterone on day 21 (or 7 days prior to expected menses)
Serum anti-Müllerian hormone (AMH) and antral follicle count
